Article Title: 'We call it kidnapping': CJP's Ashutosh Ranka calls Assam Police action completely illegal
Article Text:
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Ashutosh Ranka . (PTI Photo)

CJP to begin nationwide protest from Oct 2

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka, who was detained along with several party leaders alleged on Monday that the Assam Police action was "completely illegal."Ranka, who was later released, alleged that CJP members were picked up from private property without being informed of the grounds for their detention.Ranka alleged that the police failed to provide a specific reason for the action. “It wasn't a detention. It was completely illegal because they picked us up from private property. We don't call this detention; we call it kidnapping,” he said.“When we asked the police on what grounds we were detained, their only reply was, 'Sir, we have orders from above, so we arrested you, detained you.' And even after that, when we continuously asked while we were there, they couldn't give us any other reason,” Ranka alleged.He also accused Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma of attempting to suppress the organisation's activities.“The government's intention was to bully us. Hemanta Biswa Sarma wanted to intimidate us, but Hemanta Biswa Sarma made the same mistake that Amit Shah made on July 20th. The more you suppress, the more the revolution will spread,” he said.“Now, Assam CJP will see how students and youth issues will be raised in the coming times,” Ranka added.Ranka said CJP plans to expand its activities across Assam and other Northeastern states, focusing on issues concerning students and young people.“There are many issues in Assam; there are a lot of local issues here. The condition of schools here is very poor, especially in the remote areas where most schools don't even have their own buildings,” he said.“A complete facade has been created in the name of development, but we want the country to see the reality of that development,” Ranka added. He said the organisation would also raise issues related to floods, Kaziranga and other local concerns.“All the student and youth-centric issues that the youth of Assam have been struggling with for a long time, we will work on all of them in the coming time. We will definitely go to other Northeast states. We have received a very good response, a very good support,” Ranka said.The CJP leaders were detained on Sunday shortly before the organisation's first regional volunteers' meeting in Guwahati was scheduled to begin near the Assam Secretariat.The organisation said several senior leaders and Assam-based volunteers, including Ranka, Ankit Bhardwaj and Prem Aakash, were taken to a police facility. Reports said around 30 CJP workers were detained.The CJP had described the gathering as a peaceful meeting on private property. Assam Police has not publicly provided a detailed explanation for the detentions, according to the information available.Ranka also said that CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke had initially planned to travel to Assam following the detentions but would now focus on preparations for the organisation's proposed October 2 protest over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and its demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.“Abhijit's plan was based on our arrest yesterday. But as I've been released, Abhijit is not coming. He is busy preparing for the protest planned for October 2nd regarding SIR and Gyanesh Kumar's resignation,” Ranka told reporters.On the demand for Kumar's resignation, Ranka said the organisation would launch a nationwide protest from October 2.“It will happen now. For 48 hours, the ball was in Gyanesh Kumar's court. Now the ball is in CJP's court. We'll start our nationwide protest from 2nd October, and we won't back down until Ganeshkumar resigns,” he added.Ranka also alleged that more than 13 crore people had been removed from electoral rolls and questioned the process of electoral boundary redrawing in Assam. These claims were made by Ranka and CJP and have not been independently established.The remarks come amid a wider political dispute over the functioning of the Election Commission and the SIR exercise. An Indian Express report cited by CJP said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections on multiple occasions over SIR-related decisions.The Election Commission has rejected allegations of internal disagreement and maintained that decisions concerning SIR were taken with the “unanimous approval of the Commission.” The detentions came after the leadership of Akhil Gogoi-led Raijor Dal met CJP leaders, including Ranka, in Guwahati.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka, who was detained along with several party leaders alleged on Monday that the Assam Police action was "completely illegal" CJP plans to expand its activities across Assam and other Northeastern states, focusing on issues concerning students and young people.

Article Title: 'No basic public safety, expressing solidarity no solution': SC pulls up system amid rising rape cases in Delhi
Article Text:
Supreme Court flags systemic gaps in Delhi’s public safety measures amid rising rape cases

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday took suo motu cognisance of recent rape cases in Delhi-NCR, saying the incidents point to a “systematic failure” by law-enforcement and public administrative authorities to ensure basic public safety.A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran directed the court registry to register a suo motu public interest litigation on the issue and list it for hearing."The reports of rape cases in Delhi-NCR starkly underline a systematic failure on the part of the law enforcement and the public administrative authorities to guarantee basic public safety," news agency PTI quoted the bench saying.The court said the incidents brought back “painful parallels” with the 2012 Nirbhaya case and raised questions over whether law-enforcement mechanisms had made meaningful progress since then."One cannot help but draw painful parallels with the 2012 Nirbhaya case, raising the question of whether systemic law-enforcement mechanisms have made any meaningful progress in the decade since then," Bar and Bench quoted Justice Pardiwala saying.The bench said the right to live with dignity and without fear of violence is an intrinsic part of the fundamental right to life and personal liberty guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution.It said public spaces such as parks, roads, buses, metro stations, subways and footbridges cannot be allowed to become high-risk zones because of inadequate lighting, poor surveillance, lack of patrolling or other preventable administrative deficiencies.The court's observations came against the backdrop of multiple sexual assault cases reported in the national capital.A 16-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped by the conductor and driver of a sleeper bus after boarding it in Greater Noida on August 4. She was later abandoned near Kashmere Gate in Old Delhi, over 40 km away. Both accused have been arrested.The Supreme Court also said statements by public authorities and elected representatives expressing concern over such incidents, while understandable, do not address the larger question of institutional accountability.“Expressing solidarity is not a solution to this social evil,” the bench said, calling for a measurable response and accountability from authorities responsible for preventing crime, maintaining public order and protecting vulnerable people.The court's intervention also follows the August 4 gang-rape of a 16-year-old girl on a sleeper bus in Greater Noida. The teenager was allegedly assaulted by the bus conductor and driver and abandoned near Kashmere Gate, over 40 km away. Both accused have been arrested.
Article Summary: Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran directed the court registry to register a suo motu public interest litigation on the issue. The court said the incidents brought back “painful parallels” with the 2012 Nirbhaya case and raised questions over whether law-enforcement mechanisms had made meaningful progress.

Article Title: Balakot to Sindoor, India gave befitting reply: PM Modi on Pakistan terror
Article Text:
PM Modi’s stern message to Pakistan: ‘Time for sponsoring terror to go unpunished is long gone’

'Zero-tolerance terror policy has borne results'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a stern message to Pakistan, PM Modi said on Sunday the time when its role in sponsoring terror attacks on India would go unpunished is long gone, and his govt has made it clear with its actions, including Op Sindoor, that terrorists will be given a befitting response for their sinister designs against India.Modi's message came in his 'Mann ki Baat' broadcast as India marks the 10th anniversary of the surgical strikes on terror hideouts in Pakistan on Sept 28-29, 2016. "The world was astonished to see the manner in which our brave soldiers crossed the LoC to take action against terror. The strike demonstrated a new aspect of India's counter-terror policy. It was our decisive response to long-standing pain India had endured," he said."Over the past decade, from Balakot airstrike to Op Sindoor, India has repeatedly sent out a clear message: if terrorists dare to cast an evil eye on India, they will be met with a befitting response."Contrasting his government's targeted action against Pakistan to the approach of the previous Congress-led UPA govt, PM Narendra Modi said serial blasts had once become a common occurrence in the country. On Sept 13, 2008, serial blasts rocked Delhi and, just a few weeks later, the Mumbai terror attack stunned the country, the PM said.Demands for action against Pakistan following every terror attack used to be made then but were ignored. "Today, India pursues a zero-tolerance policy against terrorism, and we are witnessing the results of that," he said.During Op Sindoor, the Modi govt also unveiled a tougher national security doctrine, declaring that any future terror attack will be treated as an act of war. This eliminated the false distinction between terrorists and their state sponsors, it had said.Modi's message to Pakistan comes at a time when the nation is trying to airbrush its long association with terror incidents around the world, reflected in its PM Shehbaz Sharif's recent claims at the United Nations General Assembly about its role and sacrifices in combating terrorism.In his UNGA address, foreign minister S Jaishankar had snubbed Pakistan, calling it a "serial practitioner of terrorism" and asserting that India will continue to exercise its right to defend itself against terror threats.
Article Summary: Modi's message came in his 'Mann ki Baat' broadcast as India marks the 10th anniversary of the surgical strikes on terror hideouts in Pakistan on Sept 28-29, 2016. "The world was astonished to see the manner in which our brave soldiers crossed the LoC to take action against terror," he said.

NEW DELHI: Around 1,500 pilgrims stranded on the Kedarnath route near Chirbasa were safely rescued and escorted to Gaurikund after a landslide blocked the route late Sunday night, officials said.The pilgrims were stranded around three kilometres from Gaurikund after a landslide hit the route near Chirbasa, news agency ANI reported.The Rudraprayag District Control Room (DCR) informed Sonprayag Police about the situation late on September 27, following which the SDRF Sonprayag team, led by Sub-Inspector Ashish Dimri, rushed to the spot.Prioritising the safety of the pilgrims, the rescue teams carefully assisted them across the affected stretch. Around 1,500 pilgrims were brought safely to the other side of the landslide zone and escorted towards Gaurikund.The operation was carried out despite continued rockfall and the risk of further landslides in the area. Rescue personnel coordinated the movement of pilgrims to ensure they crossed the dangerous stretch safely.The coordinated efforts of the SDRF, NDRF and DDRF helped ensure that all the stranded pilgrims were safely evacuated from the affected area.Officials said the rescue operation was successfully completed despite the challenging conditions at the site.
Article Summary: Around 1,500 pilgrims stranded on the Kedarnath route near Chirbasa were safely rescued. Article Title: Stone pelting, tear gas and clashes with police: Why Ujjain is on the boil
Article Text:
The demolition is part of a larger road-widening exercise in Ujjain.

What happened at the site

City Qazi appeals for peace

Road widening for Simhastha

Ujjain prepares for 2028 gathering

NEW DELHI: Tensions rose in Ujjain on Monday as protesters clashed with police during demonstrations over development work in the city. Police were deployed in large numbers around the Shahi Masjid Complex as sporadic protests and stone pelting were reported in the area.The clashes erupted after the demolition of a portion of the Shahi Masjid as part of a road-widening project. The work is linked to preparations for the Simhastha Kumbh Mela in 2028, with authorities planning a major infrastructure overhaul ahead of the religious gathering.Police used tear gas shells to control a crowd in the city as stone pelting occurred when a large group of people clashed with them at the spot where a portion of Shahi Masjid was planned to be demolished.Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel has been deployed at the spot.SP Pradeep Sharma said: "Police personnel present at the scene responded by using tear gas and mild force to disperse the crowd. Leaders from the Muslim community are also issuing video messages urging calm.""All communities and sections of society are continuously extending their cooperation and support in their respective areas. Even today, the demolition work, initiated by the mosque committee itself, is underway at the Shahi Masjid.As a precautionary measure, a full security perimeter has been established, and entry is prohibited for everyone. However, certain miscreants attempted to create a disturbance and resorted to stone-pelting. The police personnel present at the scene responded by using tear gas and mild force to disperse the crowd," he said.Sharma said the cops utilised tear gas to manage the situation and that "entire area is being monitored via CCTV and drones".The officer futher said: "We will now identify the perpetrators using CCTV and drone footage and register FIRs against those found involved. An attempt to block the road was also made by some women; however, after being counseled and shown video footage of the situation, they withdrew the blockade. The road is open. I appeal to everyone to please cooperate; if anyone engages in such activities, strict action will be taken against them. As you can all see, this entire undertaking is being carried out by the committee itself, with everyone's consent."Protesters tried to move through narrow lanes towards the area, with some women seen being pushed forward as the crowd attempted to proceed. Stones were also thrown at police personnel deployed to maintain order.The situation remained tense as security forces stayed at the spot to prevent further escalation.Congress MP Imran Pratapgarhi, meanwhile, criticised the demolition and urged the Madhya Pradesh government to take public sentiment into account."The administrative efforts to demolish the Ujjain Shahi Masjid under the pretext of road widening should be a bit more sensitive. Demolishing a 600-year-old heritage site just for road widening and development in the name of progress is the height of hatred. It has come to my notice that when the matter is pending in court, what message does the administration intend to send by repeatedly laying siege to the masjid? Thousands of youth in Ujjain are continuously raising their voices on this issue. My request to the Ujjain administration is to respect public sentiments and acquire the necessary land for road widening from the other side. Demolishing such a historically significant heritage site cannot be considered a normal event under any circumstances," the Congress MP said.Qazi Khaliqur Rahman appealed to members of the Muslim community to maintain peace and urged them not to gather unnecessarily in markets or venture towards market areas.In a statement, the City Qazi urged people not to pay heed to rumours and remain inside their homes, maintaining that the issue concerning the mosque had already been resolved during the night.“The members of the community are informed not to stand unnecessarily in the markets or go towards the market areas. The issue related to the mosque was resolved during the night itself. There is no such matter that requires anyone to come out,” he said.The demolition is part of a larger road-widening exercise in Ujjain. Authorities have identified 272 structures for demolition as preparations intensify for the 2028 Simhastha gathering.Earlier, chief minister Mohan Yadav had participated in demolition work at his ancestral home. He said giving up the property had been emotionally difficult but was necessary for the wider development project."This is the place where I grew up, playing and running around, and now I am stepping forward to dismantle it with my own hands. It certainly has an emotional impact. However, if it is necessary for the administration and essential for the Simhastha, then this sacrifice must be made. I am satisfied that we are all doing this together," he said.Yadav said his decision was also intended to encourage other residents affected by the project to cooperate with the administration."The entire state and the country are watching this. People are demolishing their homes willingly and happily, dedicating themselves to the cause so that others may benefit greatly," he said.Ujjain Municipal Corporation chairperson Kalawati Yadav said preparations for Simhastha include several major infrastructure projects. The event is held once every 12 years on the banks of the Shipra River and is expected to draw millions of devotees."In 2028, Ujjain will host the Simhastha Mela, one of the world's largest spiritual gatherings, held every 12 years on the banks of the Shipra River. Extensive preparations are underway, including around 29 kilometres of new ghats, a diversion project, dams and other infrastructure works to improve the city. With millions of devotees expected, road widening has become essential," she said.The road-widening project is part of the wider redevelopment plan aimed at improving Ujjain's infrastructure and handling the expected influx of pilgrims during the 2028 Simhastha Mela.
Article Summary: Police used tear gas shells to control a crowd in the city as stone pelting occurred. The clashes erupted after the demolition of a portion of the Shahi Masjid as part of a road-widening project. The work is linked to preparations for the Simhastha Kumbh Mela in 2028.

Article Title: SIR row: Nadda backs EC, sends message to Rahul Gandhi and opposition
Article Text:
Nadda​ accused the oppn of repeatedly raising allegations despite responses from the Election Commission.

Kharge demands CEC's resignation

Rahul Gandhi's allegations over SIR

NEW DELHI: Union minister JP Nadda on Monday attacked the opposition and leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi over the SIR row surrounding the Election Commission , saying, “repeating a lie a hundred times does not make it the truth”.Nadda also targeted Aam Aadmi Party chief Arvind Kejriwal, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, accusing them of attempting to “malign and weaken” the country's autonomous and constitutional institutions.Speaking to reporters, Nadda took a direct aim at the Congress leader saying, “Rahul Gandhi, listen carefully: repeating a lie a hundred times does not make it the truth; the truth cannot be defeated.”“For Rahul Gandhi, Arvind Kejriwal, Akhilesh Yadav, and Mamata Banerjee, the sole agenda has become to malign and weaken the nation's autonomous and constitutional institutions. This is the same 'toolkit mentality' that hatches a new conspiracy every morning to stall the country's development: level allegations, disrupt the national atmosphere, and flee. This has become the opposition's modus operandi,” he said.“They care nothing for national security, public welfare, or the country's honor and prestige. Their only objective is to seize power, not to serve the people, but to nurture dynastic politics and reap personal benefits... The public has taught a befitting lesson to the forces seeking to create instability in the country in the past, and in the future too; every delusion and conspiracy of theirs will be shattered in the court of the people,” he added.Nadda further accused the opposition of continuing to raise allegations despite the Election Commission’s responses, saying it was attempting to create confusion and disrupt the atmosphere in the country.“Today, as the nation realizes the resolve of a 'Viksit Bharat' (Developed India) through the tireless efforts of its 1.4 billion citizens, and as India’s influence resonates across the global stage, the Congress and the entire 'INDI Alliance' are, unfortunately, frustrated and despondent at this progress..." Nadda said."Lacking policies and a vision, they are now devising new ploys to spread confusion and anarchy across the country. We all witnessed the uproar created nationwide just a few days ago over a fabricated story. Now, even after the Election Commission has exposed every lie they propagated, they are once again attempting to vitiate the atmosphere,” Nadda added.He alleged that Rahul and Kejriwal “make allegations and walk away; they have nothing to do with public interest.”The Union minister further accused the opposition of attempting to create confusion and disturb the atmosphere in the country despite lacking “intent and vision”.“We saw a few days ago how an attempt was made to disturb the atmosphere across the country on the basis of a fabricated news report. Now, even after all members of the Election Commission have responded to their allegations, they are once again engaged in efforts to vitiate the atmosphere in the country,” Nadda said.Nadda also contrasted the BJP 's approach to power with that of the opposition, saying, “For BJP, power is a means to serve the interests of 140 crore people.”He said the BJP's objective was to serve citizens and fulfil its commitment to Antyodaya, while accusing the Opposition of seeking power for dynastic politics and its own interests.Nadda's remarks came after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and other leaders demanded the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar and alleged that he was propagating the BJP's philosophy.“They will say like this only, but their own people have exposed them, and their own people are telling. Even a Chief Secretary of Kerala says, our CEC himself told him to contest the election. It means that a person who is in the highest position is propagating the BJP’s philosophy, and he has become a BJP worker. So it is clear. There is nothing. He should resign. If he has got any little moral right, he should resign from that post. And afterwards, we have to take action against him, even after resignation,” Kharge said.“I have called a working committee meeting for tomorrow, and there we'll discuss; all the working committee members will give their suggestions. And we are going to fight seriously. This issue concerns the entire country, the existence of our democracy, and the country's survival. That's why we are very serious about this issue. We'll fight, and we'll see that,” he added.The political row comes amid opposition criticism of the Election Commission's handling of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Rahul Gandhi had earlier alleged that the 2024 Lok Sabha and assembly elections were “all rigged” and demanded the immediate resignation of Gyanesh Kumar.He also accused the CEC of “match-fixing elections”, citing a news channel report claiming that Kumar had approached former Kerala chief secretary Jiji Thomson to contest the 2026 Assembly elections on a BJP ticket.The Election Commission, meanwhile, clarified that a letter sent to the Cabinet Secretary that had drawn scrutiny related to the functioning of an officer on deputation to the poll body and not to any policy matter.The row also follows an Indian Express report that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months on decisions and orders related to SIR and other electoral matters. The reported objections included issues concerning Form 6, voter deletions and access to electoral-roll databases.The poll body rejected the suggestion that these objections amounted to institutional dissent over final decisions, saying operational queries, inputs and suggestions raised during the draft stage were part of its standard administrative and decision-making process.The Election Commission maintained that all decisions taken by it, including those related to SIR, were unanimous and had the approval of all three commissioners, PTI reported.Opposition parties, including the Congress, CPI, CPI(M), Trinamool Congress and Shiv Sena (UBT), have demanded Kumar's resignation.Meanwhile, CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya said an INDIA bloc meeting is expected on September 30 to discuss the SIR exercise and the functioning of the Election Commission.
Article Summary: Union minister JP Nadda on Monday attacked the opposition and leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi over the SIR row. He said, “repeating a lie a hundred times does not make it the truth; the truth cannot be defeated” He accused the opposition of attempting to create confusion and disturb the atmosphere in the country despite lacking “intent and vision”

Rape claim, campus unrest and midnight clashes: What happened at LPU

Police deploy over 2,000 personnel

Clashes, arson and highway blockade

Rape case registered, SIT formed

NEW DELHI: Students of Lovely Professional University (LPU) in Punjab’s Phagwara went on a rampage on Sunday, vandalising property and blocking NH-44 during protests over claims that an outsider raped a female student on the university campus. The protests later turned violent as students clashed with police, damaged and set fire to vehicles, and pelted stones at security personnel. Several policemen were injured.The university has suspended regular classes for 10 days from September 28 and postponed mid-term examinations until further notice. Heavy police deployment has been made on the campus, while students have started leaving for their homes.Classes suspended, exams postponedFollowing the violence, LPU suspended regular classes for 10 days from September 28 and postponed mid-term examinations until further notice.The administration appealed to students to remain calm, follow official instructions and stay connected for further updates.Several rounds of talks between protesting students and the university management remained inconclusive.Vice Chancellor Sandhu assured students that their genuine grievances would be addressed.The protesters demanded that LPU Founder-Chancellor Ashok Mittal, who is also a BJP Rajya Sabha MP, visit the protest site and assure them that their concerns would be resolved. They also sought that access to the University Management System not be blocked and that students not be victimised for participating in the protest.A large police force led by ADGP M F Farooqui entered the LPU campus after the violence escalated. More than 2,000 personnel have been deployed to maintain security through the night, Farooqui said.“We will ensure security on the campus throughout the night... A force of over 2,000 personnel is currently deployed here. Law and order has been fully maintained and restored... The process is ongoing, and we are working to keep the situation under control. I cannot provide further details at this moment. To the families whose daughters are staying in the hostel here: please do not worry; everyone is safe... The atmosphere here is completely calm, and the university students are also cooperating with us in restoring peace. ..,” he said.Jalandhar Police Commissioner Satinder Singh said reports of disturbances in the hostels were rumours and that all hostels had been checked.“First of all, reports of disturbances in the hostels were merely rumours. All hostels have been checked, and there are no issues. Traffic has resumed, and the situation is normal. Other matters will be resolved through discussions with the students... Overall, the atmosphere is fine, and any minor issues will be addressed... Please inform the families that all students are safe and there is no cause for concern,” Singh said.DIG (Jalandhar Range) Naveen Singla also said the situation had been brought under control and that traffic movement on NH-44 would soon be restored.Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann has directed strict action against those responsible for the unrest at Lovely Professional University (LPU), the Chief Minister’s Office said.Mann also directed Director General of Police Gaurav Yadav to visit the spot and assess the situation.The protest began near Girls' Hostel-3 around 1 am on Sunday after students alleged that a female student had been raped by a plumber three days earlier. They also claimed the hostel warden had been informed but no action was taken.The protesters blocked NH-44 outside the university from around 8 am, causing long queues of stranded vehicles. Police later attempted to clear the blockade, but students allegedly threw water bottles at them and clashed with personnel.Police resorted to a mild lathi charge, following which students moved towards the campus and continued to pelt stones at police vehicles. Two police vehicles were set on fire, while four to five vehicles were damaged, according to Jalandhar Rural SSP Harvinder Singh Virk.Viral videos showed damaged property, vehicles and an ATM kiosk on the campus. Some students were also seen climbing onto a decommissioned MiG-23UM aircraft and a military tank installed on the premises.A truck driver, Vikas Yadav, said, “We have been stranded since 7 AM; there is no sign of things opening up yet... We are extremely distressed... We have had to abandon our vehicles and flee...”Police said an FIR had been registered against an unknown person based on a complaint by the students and a special investigation team had been formed.Singla said the girl was staying in Hostel No. 3 and had returned to her home after students alleged that no action had been taken on the matter. He said the investigation would involve student representatives.“We will analyse forensic samples, CCTV camera footage, call records, etc., before reaching a conclusion,” Singla said.The DIG also said students had demanded that the hostel staff comprise only women, adding that the management would address the demand.Asked about another death, Singla said a female student from Telangana studying at LPU had died by suicide 15 days earlier. “If the students say that there was foul play, action will be taken,” he said.LPU Vice Chancellor Jaspal Singh Sandhu said the university was not aware of any such rape incident but would cooperate with the investigation.LPU management has denied the rape allegations, with Registrar Monica Gulati saying certain “anti-social elements” were spreading “false, baseless and fabricated” claims.The university released a video featuring three female students identified as residents of Room No. 504 of the hostel. In the video, the students said no rape had taken place in their room and asked police and other students not to disturb them.Gulati introduced the video by saying, “I would like you to hear what the girls residing in room number 504 of GH3 told us.”The first student said, “So, we are the residents of room number 504. Nothing of that sort happened in our room; we have been living here for the past two months. Please, police and students, do not bother us. Nothing like that happened in our room, and we are not involved in this at all.”The second student said, “We have been extremely distressed today, and if we face further trouble, we will involve our parents. Please do not harass us.”The third added, “And the police should also stop coming to our room repeatedly; otherwise, we will call our parents.”Gulati later said, “The only conclusion to be drawn from all this is that anti-social elements and individuals with vested interests are behind this.”The opposition Congress criticised the AAP government over the law and order situation in Punjab.“What is happening at LPU is deeply concerning. If students have serious questions or concerns about any incident, they deserve transparent, impartial and time-bound answers, not rumours or suppression. The violence is a testament to the failed law and order situation in Punjab,” state Congress chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring said.“NH-44 has been blocked since the morning, yet not a single representative from the AAP government has bothered to meet the students and hear their grievances,” Warring said.
Article Summary: Students of Lovely Professional University (LPU) in Punjab’s Phagwara went on a rampage on Sunday, vandalising property and blocking NH-44 during protests over claims that an outsider raped a female student. The protests later turned violent as students clashed with police, damaged and set fire to vehicles, and pelted stones at security personnel. More than 2,000 personnel have been deployed to maintain security through the night.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu govt rolls back law and order department’s RTI exemption amid backlash
Article Text:
Tamil Nadu govt received backlash even from member of its ally Congress over the notification

What was the notification?

The backlash

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe the government's initial exemption of the Public (Law and Order) Department from the RTI Act was justified? Yes, for security reasons No, it restricts transparency 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

The Tamil Nadu government on Sunday withdrew its notification exempting the Public (Law and Order) Department from the Right to Information Act, hours after issuing the Gazette notification that classified the department as an "Intelligence and Security Organisation".The rollback came after the move drew criticism from political leaders, including Congress's Karti P Chidambaram and BJP's Tamilisai Soundararajan. The government, however, did not publicly cite a specific reason for issuing the exemption or explain why it was withdrawn. An official communication later confirmed that the order issued under Section 24(4) of the RTI Act had been rescinded, reported ANI.The original notification, issued by the Human Resources Management Department and published in the state Gazette, used the power available to state governments under Section 24(4) of the RTI Act. The provision allowed a state government to notify an organisation established by it as an intelligence or security organisation, thereby taking it outside the normal scope of the RTI Act.Tamil Nadu's notification designated its Public (Law and Order) Department as such an organisation. Had it remained in force, routine RTI access to a broad range of records held by the department would have been restricted.The records covered included information relating to communal and caste clashes, political agitations, police action and custody, deaths of prisoners, police firing, inquiries into law-and-order incidents and requests for withdrawal of cases arising from political or communal tensions.The exemption was not absolute. Section 24 specifically preserves access to information relating to allegations of corruption and human-rights violations, subject to the procedure prescribed under the Act.The notification itself invoked Section 24(4) and classified the department as an intelligence and security organisation. The government has not, in the material available publicly gave a detailed explanation for why the Public (Law and Order) Department was brought under this provision.The department handles sensitive law-and-order and policing-related matters, which appears to be the basis on which the exemption was framed. But that is distinct from saying that the government officially justified the move on a particular security ground. The notification, as reported, simply exercised the statutory power under Section 24(4).The proposed exemption would have affected access to records concerning issues such as police firing, custodial deaths, torture, communal and caste clashes and politically sensitive cases, prompting criticism that the move could reduce transparency.Karti Chidambaram initially criticised the decision, saying it "does not set a good precedent" and recalling that the RTI Act was enacted by the UPA government to strengthen democratic accountability."The Law and Order Department handles crucial matters such as examining inquiry reports on police firing, custodial deaths, torture, and deaths of remand prisoners, security-related detention cases, communal and caste clash reports, requests for withdrawal of politically sensitive cases and matters relating to sanction of prosecution for defamatory articles, news items, and speeches. This crucial information is now being shielded from the public. Such rollbacks are not in line with transparent governance. RTI must be expanded, not restricted," Chidambaram posted on X.After the government withdrew the notification, he welcomed the decision, saying: "My unsolicited & friendly advice to the TVK Government & CMO Tamil Nadu — don't let bureaucrats set the tone, tenor & direction of the administration."BJP's Tamilisai Soundararajan also criticised the original notification, saying: "So they are afraid of meeting the press, they are afraid of meeting the people, and they are afraid of the legal procedures. If you are free and fair, why are you afraid of RTI?" She called the move "undemocratic" and said it should be "highly condemned."With the withdrawal of the notification, the Public (Law and Order) Department is no longer covered by the newly created exemption.The RTI Act, 2005, establishes a legal framework for citizens to access information held by public authorities, subject to exemptions specified in the law.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu government withdraws notification exempting Public (Law and Order) Department from the Right to Information Act. Government did not publicly cite a specific reason for issuing the exemption or explain why it was withdrawn. Move drew criticism from political leaders, including Congress's Karti P Chidambaram and BJP's Tamilisai Soundararajan.

Article Title: 'Marriage does not advance a child’s age': Delhi HC rejects Muslim personal law defence in POCSO case
Article Text:
'A person who is sixteen before the ceremony remains sixteen afterwards,' said Justice Narula

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has refused to quash a POCSO case against a man who married a 16-year-old girl, holding that a marriage claimed to be valid under Muslim personal law cannot shield an adult from prosecution for sexual intercourse with a wife below 18.Justice Sanjeev Narula said the statutory age of 18 under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) cannot be replaced by the concept of puberty under personal law. “Put simply, marriage does not advance a child’s age. A person who is sixteen before the ceremony remains sixteen afterwards," he said, as quoted by ANI.The court was dealing with a petition filed by Bilal and another seeking quashing of FIR No. 189/2026 registered at Darya Ganj Police Station under Section 64(1) of the BNS and Section 6 of the POCSO Act . The petitioners had also sought disciplinary action against police officials and compensation for alleged false implication and harassment.According to the judgment, the girl was born on September 19, 2008, and married Bilal on December 20, 2024, when she was 16 years and three months old. Bilal was born on January 1, 1997 and was nearly 28 at the time. The couple subsequently lived together and the girl became pregnant. By May 2026, she was around eight months pregnant. Her age came to the notice of authorities when she visited a government hospital during her pregnancy.The foetus later died in utero and the girl delivered a stillborn child on June 6, 2026. The judgment records that an order was subsequently obtained from the Sub-Divisional Magistrate for exhumation of the child for DNA profiling and collection of evidence.The FIR was not based on an allegation made by the girl herself. She maintained that the marriage had taken place with the consent of both families, that she had married of her own free will and that physical relations began after the marriage. She also supported Bilal during his bail proceedings and expressed a desire to have him by her side during her pregnancy.The petitioners argued that under Muslim personal law, a Muslim of sound mind who has attained puberty is competent to marry and that, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, puberty is presumed after the age of 15. They contended that since the girl had attained puberty before the nikah, the marriage was valid and the subsequent sexual relationship could not attract criminal liability.The High Court rejected the argument, observing, “Personal law may determine whether a marriage has been contracted and the civil consequences that follow. It cannot supply an exception to a criminal law where Parliament has provided none."The court clarified that it was not deciding whether the nikah was valid, void or voidable. Even if the marriage were assumed to be valid, it said, that would not take sexual intercourse with a person below 18 outside the scope of POCSO or the BNS. The court also rejected the argument that the girl's consent or the absence of force and coercion could take the case outside POCSO.“POCSO does not confer such a power upon the child, her parents, or the Court,” it observed.The court further said that the age difference between the couple did not by itself establish guilt, but was relevant while considering whether the court should exercise its exceptional jurisdiction to terminate a POCSO prosecution at the threshold.The HC also rejected the argument that the FIR was unsustainable because neither the girl nor her family had approached the police, adding in this case, once doctors learnt that the pregnant patient was below 18, the statutory reporting mechanism was triggered, the court said.The court also rejected the petitioners' reliance on constitutional freedoms under Articles 21, 25 and 26, holding that they could not create an exception to a generally applicable penal law enacted for the protection of children.“Constitutional liberty protects choice; it does not create an exception to POCSO or the BNS,” the judgment said.The court cautioned against an interpretation that would effectively introduce a marital exception into POCSO for children below 18.Justice Narula added that, “The statutory protection would then depend not upon the age of the child, but upon whether a marriage had been arranged before the sexual relationship was discovered. That would turn the legislation on its head."“The conclusion is narrower: a marriage claimed to be valid under Muslim personal law cannot, by reason of that status alone, confer immunity from POCSO or BNS for sexual intercourse with a wife who was below 18 at the relevant time. Any other view would create, through judicial decision, an exception which Parliament has expressly excluded,” he added.The court acknowledged that individual cases may involve “affection rather than violence, and relationships rather than predation”, but said such circumstances could not permit courts to rewrite the statutory definition of an offence.Dismissing the petition, the High Court held that a marriage claimed to be valid under Muslim personal law cannot, merely because of that status, confer immunity from POCSO or the BNS for sexual intercourse with a wife who was below 18 at the relevant time.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court refused to quash a POCSO case against a man who married a 16-year-old girl. Court said marriage claimed to be valid under Muslim personal law cannot shield an adult from prosecution for sexual intercourse with a wife below 18. Justice Sanjeev Narula said the statutory age of 18 under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences cannot be replaced by the concept of puberty under personal law.

UJJAIN: A large group of people clashed with police in Ujjain at the spot where a portion of the Shahi Masjid was demolished as part of a road-widening project, news agency ANI reported on Monday.Heavy police force remains deployed in the area.The situation reportedly turned tense when some unidentified individuals began pelting stones in the area. Police personnel intervened to bring the situation under control and fired tear-gas shells to disperse the crowd.The confrontation took place as the Ujjain Municipal Corporation started removing the mosque portion falling within the proposed road alignment for the widening project ahead of Simhastha 2028.Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel are also present at the spot.Earlier, Madhya Pradesh chief minister Mohan Yadav intitaed various develoment works in Ujjain with the demolition activity carried out at his ancestral home.272 structures have been marked for demolition as part of a road-widening project in Ujjain ahead of the Simhastha 2028 fair.Speaking on the occasion, Yadav said the demolition of his childhood home carried personal significance, but was necessary for the larger cause."This is the place where I grew up, playing and running around, and now I am stepping forward to dismantle it with my own hands. It certainly has an emotional impact. However, if it is necessary for the administration and essential for the Simhastha, then this sacrifice must be made. I am satisfied that we are all doing this together," he said.He added that the gesture was meant to set an example for residents whose properties were also being affected by the project."The entire state and the country are watching this. People are demolishing their homes willingly and happily, dedicating themselves to the cause so that others may benefit greatly," he said.Ujjain Municipal Corporation Chairperson Kalawati Yadav explained the scale of preparations underway for the upcoming religious gathering, as it is one of the biggest spiritual gatherings that happens once every 12 years."In 2028, Ujjain will host the Simhastha Mela, one of the world's largest spiritual gatherings, held every 12 years on the banks of the Shipra River. With millions of devotees expected, road widening has become essential," she said.The road-widening initiative forms part of the broader infrastructure overhaul being undertaken in Ujjain to accommodate the massive influx of pilgrims expected during the Simhastha Mela in 2028.

Article Title: 'Crushed man's head with stones': How Delhi murder accused evaded arrest for 24 years
Article Text:
A man named Firoj has been arrested after evading capture for 24 years.A man named Firoj has been arrested after evading capture for 24 years.





NEW DELHI: A 24-year-long manhunt, which began with a highly decomposed body being found in a DDA forest, ended with the accused being arrested from Gurgaon by Delhi Police's Crime Branch. The accused, Firoj, had been absconding for over two decades after murdering a man to avenge an old family-related vendetta.On Feb 18, 2002, the decomposed body of 35-year-old Kalaam Ansari was found, covered with stones, inside the DDA forest near Tughlaqabad Fort. His head had been completely crushed. The deceased was identified as a resident of West Champaran, Bihar.During the investigation, police found Ansari had come to Delhi in 2001 for employment along with the murder accused, Firoj. One year later, on Feb 15, 2002, Firoj took Ansari to the forest near Tughlaqabad and crushed his head with stones, a senior police officer said.As per police, Ansari’s sister and Firoj’s brother, Saahbjan, were married and lived in the deceased’s village in West Champaran. Saahbjan had a dispute with his wife, who had refused to accompany him outside her village. Following this, Saahbjan committed suicide in front of the deceased’s house.Firoj suspected Ansari’s family had driven his brother to kill himself and had allegedly expressed his intention to take revenge.“One year after the duo came to Delhi in search of a job, Firoj took Ansari to the forest near Tughlaqabad and crushed his head with stones in 2002. He then returned to Bihar and started giving misleading information regarding the deceased’s whereabouts. When the murder came to light three days later, Firoj absconded and remained untraceable for nearly 24 years,” said DCP Harsh Indora.Considering the prolonged evasion of the accused and the heinous crime committed, Crime Branch undertook the task of tracing and arresting Firoj. Leads were developed by analysing old records, current data and sustained field efforts. After multiple visits to Bihar, 30 raids at suspected locations and a painstaking reconstruction of the accused’s trail conducted over two months, the police finally arrested Firoj from a ready-made garment factory in IMT Manesar, Gurgaon.Firoj, who is now 48 years old, had been working in the factory as a tailor for the past two years. After the murder, he had cut off ties with his native village and managed to conceal his identity for decades, and eventually shifted to Gurgaon, where he had been working at different places. He is married and has four children.Further investigation by the police is in progress.
Article Summary: A man named Firoj has been arrested after evading capture for 24 years. The accused had been absconding for over two decades after murdering a man to avenge an old family-related vendetta. On Feb 18, 2002, the decomposed body of 35-year- old Kalaam Ansari was found, covered with stones, inside the DDA forest near Tughlaqabad Fort.

Article Title: Netanyahu, holding ICC arrest warrant, wants to build case against Turkey's Erdogan; demands probe
Article Text:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan

Turkey faces criticism over treatment of Kurds

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who himself has an arrest warrant by International Criminal Court, has asked an inter-ministerial team to prepare a potential case for ICC against Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan over Turkey’s treatment of Kurds and alleged support for Hamas.According to the report by i24NEWS, Netanyahu instructed an inter-ministerial team and the director of Israel’s International Law Department to begin preparing the case.The report said the proposed legal action would focus primarily on Erdogan’s treatment of Kurdish minorities in Turkey, while also examining allegations related to Turkish government funding and support for Hamas.Netanyahu himself is subject to an ICC arrest warrant issued in November 2024 over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza.The ICC said there were reasonable grounds to believe Netanyahu was criminally responsible for alleged acts including starvation as a method of warfare, murder, persecution and other inhumane acts. Netanyahu and Israel have rejected the allegations and challenged the court’s jurisdiction.The reported move comes amid a sharp deterioration in relations between Ankara and Tel Aviv, with both governments increasingly turning to international legal and diplomatic mechanisms against each other.i24NEWS said the preparation of the case could also be linked to Turkey’s efforts to pursue action against Netanyahu through international channels.The report also said Israeli officials hoped the case might not ultimately need to be filed, with the threat of potential legal action being considered as a deterrent against further Turkish moves. Netanyahu’s office and Israel’s Justice Ministry declined to comment on the report.Turkey’s conflict with the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK) began in 1984 and has killed more than 40,000 people over four decades.Human rights groups have for years criticised Ankara over its treatment of Kurdish politicians and activists. Human Rights Watch said in its 2026 report that Turkey had yet to take steps to ensure equal rights for Kurds, amend what it described as abusive counterterrorism laws or release Kurdish political prisoners.It also highlighted the continued imprisonment of former pro-Kurdish HDP leaders Selahattin Demirtaş and Figen Yüksekdağ.The criticism also extends to local politics. Human Rights Watch and other rights groups have documented the removal of elected Kurdish mayors and their replacement by government-appointed trustees, while the European Parliament has criticised the practice as undermining local democracy.Turkey maintains that its counterterrorism measures are aimed at the PKK and other groups it considers security threats, rather than Kurds as an ethnic community. The PKK is designated as a terrorist organisation by Turkey, the US and the European Union.
Article Summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has asked an inter-ministerial team to prepare a potential case for ICC against Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan. The proposed legal action would focus primarily on Erdogan’s treatment of Kurdish minorities in Turkey, while also examining allegations related to Turkish government funding and support for Hamas.

Article Title: 'Unacceptable cynical attempt': Why US rejected Iran's ceasefire proposal
Article Text:
US rejects Iran’s Hormuz offer over demand for sanctions relief, frozen funds

US Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz said on Sunday that Washington rejected Iran’s proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz because Tehran sought sanctions relief and access to “billions in frozen assets” before talks on its nuclear programme.“They were asking for everything up front, with a promise that they would then talk,” Waltz said on CNN’s “State of the Union” when asked what US President Donald Trump objected to.In a separate interview with NBC, Waltz called Iran’s proposal “a pretty cynical attempt to put something on the table that they knew was unacceptable.” He said the US would ultimately need to reach “some type of agreement” with Iran, while stressing that Trump would keep all “options on the table”.Waltz said Iran’s seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz included a “request to have access to billions in frozen funds and a request for the lifting of sanctions”.“These aren’t just the United States’s sanctions,” Waltz said. “These are global sanctions. It’s worth reminding people that this is the world’s position.”Waltz also pointed to Iran’s nuclear programme, saying that “there has been not one, not two, but seven UN Security Council resolutions over the last 20 years saying Iran cannot and should not have a nuclear weapons programme”.He added that the International Atomic Energy Agency had referred Iran to the Security Council “for violations”, including Tehran’s refusal to allow inspectors into the country and provide “proper oversight of their enrichment”.Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi later disputed Waltz’s account of the proposal.“I am surprised that the ambassador is talking about a seven-day plan, as he has not read it,” Araghchi said. “Maybe he has not been given a copy.”However, Araghchi has also said Iran remained open to diplomacy while warning that Tehran was prepared for renewed hostilities.“We are fully prepared for the war to be resumed. We stand firm in the face of any new aggression, even if it comes to a doomsday war. We don’t care about U.S. midterm elections. We care about our national interests. At the same time, we stand ready for diplomacy. It is up to President Trump to choose,” he said.US President Donald Trump has rejected Iran’s seven-day ceasefire proposal and told aides he expects US bombing of Iran to resume after the November midterm elections, according to US officials cited by The Washington Post.Under Tehran’s proposal, the US would lift its naval blockade of Iranian ports, ease sanctions on Iranian oil exports and observe a ceasefire that would include Lebanon. In return, Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume negotiations with Washington on its nuclear programme.Trump has said Tehran is seeking a deal after the midterm elections that would dismantle its nuclear programme. However, according to The Washington Post, he remains privately skeptical that Iran would meet his demands and has told aides that renewed bombing is likely.However, Trump expressed confidence that the conflict with Iran would be won “very soon”, while acknowledging that fresh US military strikes before the November midterm elections were “possible”.Speaking to Fox News on the sidelines of the PGA Tour Presidents Cup on Sunday (local time), Trump said an end to the confrontation would lead to a sharp fall in global oil prices. He reiterated that preventing Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon remained the primary US objective.“I think what's going to happen is we're going to win this war very soon, and as soon as we win it, the oil will go down, way down to what it was before the war,” Trump told Fox News.With Iran maintaining its position despite Trump’s threat of further military action and rejection of its peace proposal, tensions in West Asia could intensify after the US midterm elections.
Article Summary: US Ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz said Tehran sought sanctions relief and access to “billions in frozen assets” before talks on its nuclear programme. Waltz called Iran’s proposal “a pretty cynical attempt to put something on the table that they knew was unacceptable” He said the US would ultimately need to reach ‘some type of agreement’ with Iran.

Article Title: 'Want to score well': Friend says Sahil Wakode told her in 'last call' he was caught cheating
Article Text:
According to police, Wakode told her during the call that his thermodynamics theory paper had gone poorly.





MUMBAI: The Mumbai crime branch probing the abetment to suicide of IIT-Bombay student Sahil Wakode has recorded the statement of a friend, who told investigators that she was the last person to speak to him on the phone.According to police, Wakode told her during the call that his thermodynamics theory paper had gone poorly and that he was worried as he had wanted to score well. He also told her that he had been caught cheating during the exam, they said.The friend, who is among at least six students whose statements have been recorded so far, told police that Wakode appeared stressed during their conversation. However, investigators have so far not found any clear indication of stress or distress in the material examined during the probe.Wakode (22), a second-year BTech student, was found dead in his hostel room hours after the exam on Sept 18.Investigators are reconstructing his movements after he left the exam hall. CCTV footage has established that Wakode left the hall after he was asked to do so and returned later.The CCTV footage has been sent for forensic analysis. Investigators are also examining Wakode’s locked iPhone, hoping to retrieve his last calls, messages and other data.Experts have so far been unable to access the phone because of its password.Police said they are currently recording the statements of students and other witnesses and will subsequently record the statement of Prof Suryanarayana Doolla, who was present during the exam.Wakode’s parents made an emotional appeal to IIT-B students to continue their protest and sought preservation of any evidence relating to the death. In another video message addressed to students, Wakode’s father said on Sunday he had been unable to enter the campus despite visiting it two or three times. He reiterated that he planned to begin a hunger strike at Azad Maidan from Monday, demanding access to the institute and justice for his son.
Article Summary: Mumbai crime branch probing the abetment to suicide of IIT-Bombay student Sahil Wakode has recorded the statement of a friend. Wakode (22), a second-year BTech student, was found dead in his hostel room hours after the exam on Sept 18.

Article Title: Toll soars to 81 as UP is lashed by 775% excess rainfall in 48 hours
Article Text:
In 48 hours, torrential rainfall hit Uttar Pradesh, causing devastating consequences that claimed 81 lives and injured 62





LUCKNOW: At least 81 people have lost their lives, and 62 others have been injured so far as incessant rain battered large parts of Uttar Pradesh between Sept 25 and Sept 27, causing widespread destruction across the state.The state has also recorded the deaths of 154 animals, while damage to crops is still being assessed.According to a situation report prepared by UP Relief Commissioner Hrishikesh Bhaskar Yashod’s office, Sitapur was the worst-affected district in terms of fatalities, reporting seven deaths. Lakhimpur Kheri, Bahraich and Balrampur recorded five deaths each, while Ayodhya, Maharajganj and Gorakhpur reported four fatalities each.Among the injured, Hardoi reported the highest number of injuries at seven, followed by Mainpuri and Shravasti with five each. Four people in Barabanki and three each in Sitapur and Lakhimpur Kheri also suffered injuries in rain-related incidents.A total of 154 animal deaths were reported across the state, with Hardoi accounting for the highest number at 28.Property damage was extensive, with 2,254 houses reported to be damaged.The report said that Uttar Pradesh received an average of 66.5 mm of rainfall during the 48-hour period against the normal 7.6 mm, representing 775% excess rainfall.Out of the state’s 75 districts, 56 recorded “large excess” rainfall. Farrukhabad registered the highest rainfall deviation at 7,385% above normal, followed by Kannauj (5,664%), Shahjahanpur (4,408%), Hamirpur (4,240%) and Mahoba (4,100%).“Assessment of crop losses is still underway as district administrations continue to carry out rescue, relief and damage assessment operations in affected areas,” Yashod said.
Article Summary: In 48 hours, torrential rainfall hit Uttar Pradesh, causing devastating consequences. At least 81 people have lost their lives, and 62 others have been injured so far. The state has also recorded the deaths of 154 animals, while damage to crops is still being assessed.

Article Title: ‘Rape-suicide’ rumour, arson, exams deferred, highway blocked: What we know so far about LPU protests
Article Text:
Following unsettling rumors of a student's alleged rape and suicide, Lovely Professional University witnessed violent protests.





JALANDHAR: Violent protests erupted at the Lovely Professional University campus in Phagwara on Saturday night following rumours of the rape and suicide of a female student at a hostel -- the pattern uncanny similar to protests that rocked Chitkara University a day earlier though police deny any linkage.Protesters alleged that a student died by suicide after being raped by a varsity worker in a room in girls’ hostel No. 3 on Sept 23, and that university authorities suppressed it. LPU authorities have rejected the “false and fabricated rumours” and blamed anti-social elements for the mischief.Jalandhar Range DIG Naveen Singla said police have registered an FIR on a statement from the protesting students and set up an SIT. No one is named in the FIR and police are scanning CCTV footage of the hostel.Protests subsided for a while on Sunday but flared up again in the evening, with vehicles being torched and wrecked on the highway, leading to a police lathicharge. The protest was raging at the time this report was filed. The blockade has thrown traffic to parts of Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir out of gear.According to sources, messages of the ‘rape and suicide’ began circulating on Saturday night and boarders started gathering outside a girls’ hostel.Police said students living in rented accommodations outside the campus soon joined them. As the numbers swelled, the protestors turned violent.They went on the rampage, targeting the administrative buildings and damaging the campus mall. Protesters took away laptops and other gadgets, set fire to motorcycles, and began posting videos of the arson on social media.Then, around 2 am, hundreds of them blocked the National Highway stretch between Jalandhar and Phagwara. As flames rose in the background, protesters climbed atop a MiG-23 and a tank donated to the university by the military.Police managed to persuade the students to lift the blockade early in the morning, but they again blocked it.As police officers negotiated with the students, some of them told DIG Singla about the alleged suicide of a female student from Telangana around a fortnight back. Singla said the parents of the student had come to LPU and police had sent her mobile phone for forensic examination. Further action would be based on the findings of the lab report, he said.After students refused to lift the blockade, police resorted to lathicharge around 8 pm and students retaliated by stone-pelting. Both cops and some students sustained injuries. DIG Singla’s vehicle was damaged along with a few other vehicles, including a journalist’s car. At least one vehicle was torched. Some of those indulging in violence had covered their faces.Several students alleged that it was outsiders who indulged in loot, arson and vandalism. Some masked men were captured in videos during the protest.“Police officers tried a lot to persuade students to lift the blockade and apprised them about the investigation but they refused to relent. Force was used in a restrained way to clear the NH,” special DGP (law and order) Parveen Sinha said.Kapurthala SSP Gaurav Toora said the pattern matched the trouble at Chitkara University, as trouble at LPU also started with hearsay of the rape of a student, but nobody knew about her or the accused. Special DGP Sinha said that so far there did not appear to be any linkages between the protests at Chitkara University and LPU.On Sunday afternoon, LPU put out a video statement by three students who live in the hostel room mentioned by protesters. They said that no such incident took place in their room, and that they felt harassed by the repeated queries by police.The university issued a statement denying the allegations. “It has come to our notice that certain anti-social elements are spreading completely false, baseless and fabricated rumours through social media and other channels, thereby creating unnecessary confusion among students and attempting to disturb the peaceful academic environment of the university,” said LPU registrar Monica Gulati on Sunday morning.“The manner in which such false and misleading information is being systematically circulated appears to be a deliberate and concerted attempt to malign the reputation of the university and tarnish its image. The University categorically clarifies that there is no truth in the rumours presently being circulated. Students, parents and members of the public are requested not to believe, circulate or amplify such rumours. They should rely upon information communicated through official channels of the University only,” Gulati said.LPU vice-chancellor Jaspal Singh Sandhu said that they were open to the probe and would provide all necessary support to the investigators. “There is nothing to hide and such matters can’t be concealed,” he said.Classes suspended for 10 days, exams put offLovely Professional University (LPU) Sunday night announced the suspension of regular classes for 10 days and postponement of mid-term examinations until further notice. It advised students to go back to their hometowns during this period. “Students who stay back are advised to stay inside their hostels and avoid unnecessary movement...” LPU said
Article Summary: Violent protests erupted at the Lovely Professional University campus in Phagwara on Saturday night. Protesters alleged that a student died by suicide after being raped by a varsity worker in a room in girls’ hostel No. 3 on Sept 23. Police have registered an FIR on a statement from the protesting students and set up an SIT. LPU authorities have rejected the “false and fabricated rumours” and blamed anti-social elements for the mischief.

Article Title: ‘Shopping for free’: Videos show students looting LPU campus mall amid violent protest
Article Text:
Several videos from Lovely Professional University show students reportedly taking items from shops during protests.

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be the main priority after the LPU unrest? Ensuring student safety Restoring peace on campus Investigating the incident Preventing further violence 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





CHANDIGARH: Several videos emerging from Lovely Professional University (LPU) in Punjab’s Phagwara appear to show students entering shops inside the university’s Uni Mall, picking up food, gadgets and other items amid the violent protests that rocked the campus on Sunday.In one video, a voice can be heard saying “free mein shopping, shopping done” as people move around inside a store.Another video shows a person pointing towards various items in the mall and saying, “What do you need? Order now, will get everything for you in free.”Also read: LPU Student Protest Live Updates Other visuals purportedly show students eating food items inside the mall, while another set of videos shows shops and other property damaged during the unrest.The videos could not be independently verified. It was also not immediately clear from the visuals whether all those seen taking items were students of LPU.The alleged looting came as protests at LPU over claims surrounding the alleged rape of a female student escalated into violence, with protesters vandalising property, attacking police vehicles and blocking NH-44.Police said protesters pelted stones at police personnel after they were asked to clear the highway blockade on Sunday evening.Two police vehicles were set on fire and several others were damaged, officials said. A number of policemen were injured in the clashes.Also read: Students atop MiG-23, military tank Videos circulating online also show damage to shops in the campus mall, an ATM kiosk and other university property. Some protesters were seen with their faces covered.According to police, messages about an alleged rape and the death by suicide of a female student had begun circulating on social media on Saturday night, following which students gathered outside a girls’ hostel. The protest later spread to the highway and other parts of the campus.Police said an FIR had been registered based on the complaint relating to the alleged rape and an SIT had been formed. Investigators said CCTV footage, forensic samples and call records would be examined as part of the probe.LPU, however, has denied the rape allegations being circulated on campus, describing them as “false, baseless and fabricated rumours”. The university said it would cooperate with the investigation.A student claimed that the situation had gone beyond the students’ protest and alleged that outsiders and “goons” had entered the university.“The university's stand is that the students should stay safe. It is better for them to stay inside their hostels and stay safe from the locals and goons who have come. Instead of roaming outside, if they want to protest, they can do it peacefully,” the student said.The student further alleged that several students had confronted those involved in the violence and claimed that the university hall had been damaged, the CS building set on fire and the admission block vandalised.Also read: Abhijeet Dipke's 1st reaction on LPU unrest The unrest also followed discussions around the death by suicide of a Telangana student at LPU around a fortnight earlier. Police said the student’s mobile phone had been sent for forensic examination and further action would depend on the findings.The protests continued through Sunday, with students blocking NH-44 for several hours. Police eventually used a lathi charge to clear the blockade after negotiations failed, following which students allegedly retaliated with stone-pelting.Amid the violence, students were also seen climbing onto a decommissioned MiG-23 aircraft and a military tank displayed on the campus.LPU has suspended classes for 10 days from Monday and postponed midterm examinations until further notice.While some students alleged that outsiders were responsible for the looting, arson and vandalism, police said several people involved in the violence had their faces covered.The exact identities of those involved in the alleged looting and damage are expected to be established through CCTV footage and the police investigation.
Article Summary: Several videos from Lovely Professional University show students reportedly taking items from shops during protests. The alleged looting came as protests at LPU over claims surrounding the alleged rape of a female student escalated into violence. Police said protesters pelted stones at police personnel after they were asked to clear the highway blockade.

Article Title: Kolkata woman 'assaulted, abused' at at five-star hotel nightclub, JW Marriott says venue is third-party run
Article Text:
A young woman reported an incident of assault and wrongful restraint at a nightclub early Sunday morning. (File pic)





KOLKATA: Pragati Maidan cops have arrested a 24-year-old man for allegedly wrongfully restraining, physically assaulting, and outraging the modesty of a young woman at a nightclub inside a prominent five star hotel located along the EM Bypass near Science City in the early hours of Sunday.The arrested suspect has been identified as Mohammed Rafey Azim (24), a resident of Bhukailash Road in Kidderpore and Tiljala Road in the Beniapukur area.According to police, the incident occurred around 2 am on Sunday, when the 20-year-old complainant, a resident of New Alipore , visited the disco located inside the five star property along with a group of eight friends.The victim stated in her complaint that while they were at the venue, the accused, aided and abetted by others, confronted her group. The suspect allegedly subjected the complainant to wrongful restraint, physically assaulted her, and used extremely filthy and abusive language intended to insult her modesty. Following the altercation and physical assault, the accused and his aides fled the scene.The police were alerted through an emergency call at the Dial 100 control room. A team from Pragati Maidan PS immediately rushed to the place of occurrence.Cops said the five star hotel administration helped them in collecting evidence when requested.According to additional CP (crime) Kunal Agarwal, cops arrested the accused as soon as they received the complaint. “After receiving the information from Toy Room Disco located inside JW Marriott Hotel through Dial 100, a team of Pragati Maidan PS visited the place and after examination requested the complainant to submit a complaint. Meanwhile, the complainant and her friends came to Pragati Maidan PS and submitted the plaint letter. On the basis of it, an FIR was started. After lodging the FIR and identifying the address of accused, a raid was conducted and the accused was arrested,” said Agarwal.Pragati Maidan Police registered charges under sections 74 (assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty), 79 (word, gesture, or act intended to insult modesty), 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt), 126(2) (wrongful restraint), and 54 (abettor present when offence is committed) of the BNS.Azim was arrested from his Tiljala Road residence around 11:40 am on Sunday.Gorav Arora, general manager, JW Marriott Kolkata, said: “Toy Room is a third-party managed outsourced venue and the hotel does not operate it. We will however continue to extend our cooperation to the concerned authorities.”
Article Summary: A young woman reported an incident of assault and wrongful restraint at a nightclub early Sunday morning. The suspect allegedly subjected the complainant to wrongful restraint, physically assaulted her, and used extremely filthy and abusive language intended to insult her modesty. Mohammed Rafey Azim was arrested from his Tiljala Road residence.

Article Title: Fake medicine racket: Prime suspect arrested at Bengaluru airport after landing from Sharjah
Article Text:
R Prashanth Babu, a medical representative, was caught at Bengaluru's Kempegowda International Airport as part of a major police operation targeting a fake drug network spanning multiple states
