Forged labels:





BENGALURU: A special investigation team probing a multi-state fake drug racket arrested one of its prime suspects, R Prashanth Babu, at Bengaluru's Kempegowda International Airport early Monday.Prashanth, a medical representative and resident of Papareddypalya in Bengaluru, was arrested after he landed from Sharjah around 5.30am.The arrest comes after police and health department officials busted the racket on August 18 this year. The operation was being run from an unlicensed facility near Tavarekere in Bidadi, in Ramanagara-Bengaluru South district. Drug enforcement officials and police seized spurious and expired medicines, packaging material and drug-filling equipment worth around Rs 5 crore.Police have so far arrested eight accused, including alleged kingpin Veeresh Kumar Jain, who ran the Krupa Health Care unit at Minerva Circle.The racket came to light after a labourer in C K Tandya village near Dodderi noticed discarded medicine waste, including vials, tubes and powder, dumped in a field. He alerted Shivaraj, a local police constable from Tavarekere police station.Shivaraj visited the spot in plain clothes, collected samples and informed senior officials.Based on the information, the Karnataka Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA), along with local police, raided a farmhouse in Kurubara Karenahalli near the Bidadi toll gate.Investigators found that the operators were running an unlicensed manufacturing, repackaging and relabelling unit.The racket procured cheap, substandard generic medicines, expired medicines and low-cost cancer drugs from illegal manufacturing units across multiple states, including Telangana and Himachal Pradesh.The medicines were transferred into new vials and packages at the Bidadi farmhouse.The operators allegedly used forged labels, stamps and boxes bearing the names of prominent multinational pharmaceutical brands, including Pfizer and Kupa Healthcare, to sell the medicines as expensive, premium products.
Article Summary: R Prashanth Babu, a medical representative, was arrested at Bengaluru's Kempegowda International Airport. The arrest comes after police and health department officials busted the racket on August 18 this year. The operation was being run from an unlicensed facility near Tavarekere in Bidadi, in Ramanagara- Bengaluru South district.

Article Title: ‘Harassed by math teacher for 3 months’: Ghaziabad girl dies after falling from 10th floor
Article Text:
A 13-year-old girl from Sahibabad fell from the 10th floor of a building and died.





GHAZIABAD: A 13-year-old girl died after falling from the 10th floor of a residential building in Sahibabad on Saturday night.Her family alleged that a schoolteacher had harassed her and that she had recorded everything in her diary.According to police, the deceased a resident of Gulmohar society in Sahibabad. Her father is a businessman in the city.A senior police officer said that the deceased was a student of class 7th of a private school in Sahibabad.Late on Saturday evening, the deceased had left the flat after telling her mother that she would return in a while. Shortly afterward, they were informed that she had fallen from the 10th floor.When her mother reached downstairs, a doctor living in the society was giving CPR to her daughter. After this, the student was taken by car to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared her dead during treatment after a short while.Acting on the information, police reached the spot, took the student’s body into custody and sent it for postmortem. After the postmortem on Saturday, police handed over the body to the family, and late in the evening the family performed the student’s last rites at the cremation ground on the Hindon riverbank.A family member said that the girl was harassed by her school math teacher for the last three months. She mentioned everything in her diary. Some days ago, an internal exam had been held at the school and the answer sheets had been shown to the students on Friday. She scored 30 marks in math after which she was angry and scared.Rijual, DCP of Trans-Hindon said police had not found any suicide note at her house. The family had neither lodged a complaint nor shown police any writing by the girl.“The body was sent for autopsy and reports are awaited,” he said.
Article Summary: A 13-year-old girl died after falling from the 10th floor of a residential building in Sahibabad on Saturday night. Her family alleged that a schoolteacher had harassed her and that she had recorded everything in her diary. The body was sent for autopsy and reports are awaited, police said.

Article Title: Uttarakhand CM Dhami directs officials to maintain vigilance amid red alert in several districts
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami , in view of the red alert issued by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) for the next two days, spoke to Secretary Disaster Management and Rehabilitation Vinod Kumar Suman and directed all concerned districts and departments to take necessary precautionary measures.Dhami directed officials to maintain heightened vigilance in districts under red and orange alerts, continuously monitor vulnerable areas and ensure that all arrangements for relief and rescue operations are in place in advance in case of any emergency. He also directed that district emergency operation centres remain active and weather warnings be disseminated immediately at the local level.Disaster management and rehabilitation minister Madan Kaushik also spoke to Secretary Vinod Kumar Suman and took stock of the weather situation and preparedness across the state. He directed officials to closely monitor the weather and remain fully prepared to deal with any eventuality.Following the chief minister’s directions, Secretary Vinod Kumar Suman held a meeting with all 13 districts on Friday and instructed them to remain on alert mode.According to the weather department forecast, on September 26, red alerts have been issued for five districts, orange alerts for five districts and yellow alerts for three districts.On September 27, red alerts have been issued for four districts, orange alerts for four districts and yellow alerts for five districts.On September 26, Bageshwar, Pithoragarh, Champawat, Nainital and Udham Singh Nagar are under a red alert, while Dehradun, Pauri Garhwal, Rudraprayag, Chamoli and Almora are under an orange alert. Haridwar, Uttarkashi and Tehri Garhwal are under a yellow alert.On September 27, red alerts have been issued for Dehradun, Tehri Garhwal, Pauri Garhwal and Haridwar; orange alerts for Uttarkashi, Chamoli, Nainital and Rudraprayag; and yellow alerts for Bageshwar, Almora, Champawat, Udham Singh Nagar and Pithoragarh.The weather department has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall at several places and extremely heavy rainfall at isolated places. Authorities have been asked to remain particularly vigilant in view of the possibility of landslides and road blockages in hilly areas, rising water levels in rivers and streams, and waterlogging in the plains.Suman directed all districts to continuously monitor vulnerable areas, keep district emergency operation centres operational and ensure immediate dissemination of every weather warning to the ground level.Officials have been instructed to continuously monitor water levels in rivers, streams, gad-gaderas and other water sources and make arrangements to shift people living nearby to safer locations if water levels rise. JCBs and other necessary machinery should be stationed at strategic locations along landslide-prone roads and areas so that blocked routes can be cleared at the earliest.All district emergency operation centres have been directed to remain operational round the clock, with continuous coordination among the police, SDRF, fire services, health, Public Works Department, drinking water, power and other concerned departments. Relief and rescue teams, along with necessary equipment and resources, should be deployed in vulnerable areas as required.The secretary also directed that traffic on mountain routes be regulated based on weather and road conditions and unnecessary travel in areas vulnerable to landslides and heavy rainfall be avoided. People living near rivers, streams and seasonal water channels should be regularly alerted and prevented from approaching riverbanks or entering fast-flowing waters.Special monitoring has also been ordered along the Char Dham routes, major tourist destinations and other vulnerable areas to ensure the safety of pilgrims and tourists. All arrangements should be kept ready in advance so that relief and rescue operations can begin with minimum response time in case of an emergency.Suman urged district administrations to remain fully alert and not to show any negligence in view of the prevailing weather conditions. He also appealed to the public to follow advisories issued by the weather department and district administration, avoid unnecessary travel and stay away from rivers, streams and landslide-prone areas.The State Emergency Operation Centre is continuously monitoring the weather situation. In case of any emergency, people can contact the State Emergency Operation Centre at toll-free number 1070, the District Emergency Operation Centre at 1077, or emergency services at 112.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami spoke to Secretary Disaster Management and Rehabilitation Vinod Kumar Suman. He directed officials to maintain heightened vigilance in districts under red and orange alerts. Suman urged district administrations to remain fully alert and not to show any negligence in view of the prevailing weather conditions.

Article Title: Strong waves & swell surge: Red alert issued in all coastal districts of Keralam
Article Text:
Until Incois withdraws the warning, all activities, including beach-centered tourism should be completely avoided

Kochi:





Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (Incois) has declared a red alert in all coastal districts of Keralam. The agency has warned that coastal areas of the state could experience strong waves and swell surge phenomenon.Incois has warned that there is a possibility of high waves ranging from 1.0 to 1.5 metres and sea swell along Kerala coast from 2.30am on Saturday to 2.30am on Monday. In coastal zones, especially in low-lying areas, there is a possibility of inundation and swell surge.A vigilance warning for high waves and the swell surge has been issued for Kanyakumari, Ramanathapuram, Thoothukudi, Tirunelveli coasts of Tamil Nadu and Lakshadweep coasts as well. Since there is a possibility of swell surge, fishermen and coastal residents should exercise extreme caution.Until Incois withdraws the warning, all activities, including beach-centred tourism, should be completely avoided. Fishing vessels should be safely tied and secured at the harbour. Maintaining a safe distance between vessels can avoid the risk of accidents due to collision. The safety of fishing equipment should be ensured.Trips to the beach and recreational activities in the sea should be completely avoided.
Article Summary: Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (Incois) has declared a red alert in all coastal districts of Keralam. The agency has warned that coastal areas of the state could experience strong waves and swell surge phenomenon. Until Incois withdraws the warning, all activities, including beach- centered tourism should be completely avoided.

Article Title: Trump embraces Xi as peer, alarms partners and critics
Article Text: TOI correspondent from Washington: A 48-hour state visit to the United States by China’s President Xi Jinping yielded no immediate major breakthroughs but confirmed the broad impression, in visuals and much as words, that Washington now accepts China as a peer in a new G-2 formulation.For all the talk of trade, artificial intelligence, Taiwan, Iran and strategic competition, the most consequential message of Xi’s visit may have been the choreography itself. A fawning Trump repeatedly described Xi as a friend and the relationship as a “great friendship,” with little personal reciprocity from the Chinese leader.The charitable explanation for what many critics said was Trump’s folding before Xi and muting his demands from and tirades against China was purportedly in the service of American farmers – his major voting bloc – who are getting screwed because Beijing cut down purchase of soy, corn, and other farm produce. In brief remarks during a tea ceremony, the MAGA supremo mentioned that the visit had yielded “great results” for American farmers without elaborating, but spoke of little else other than accepting Xi’s invitation to visit China.By most accounts, the summit produced a lot of optics, but little else, amid a cascade of criticism that Trump is placating China rather than confronting it over its actions inimical to US, including its tacit support for Iran.The most withering censure came from Republican Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana, who likened Xi and leaders of Russia, North Korea and Iran, to reptiles. "The chief reptile, the quarterback, is President Xi. They all lie like timeshare salesmen. You can’t trust them. I wouldn’t turn my back on any of them, even if I thought and knew they were two days dead,” Kennedy told a TV show during the visit. Even Senator Chuck Grassley, the Iowa Republican whose state is deeply dependent on agricultural exports, was sceptical about the outcome of the visit, saying that if extending the trade truce was all that emerged, the summit risked becoming a “show job" for a communist autocrat.On Taiwan, the most sensitive strategic issue between the two sides, there was no public breakthrough. Trump has continued to hold in abeyance a roughly $14 billion Taiwan weapons package that he described earlier this year as a negotiating chip with Beijing. China wants the arms sales halted; US lawmakers across party lines have urged their release.Nor were there any signs of a significant Chinese concession on Iran. Beijing has expressed interest in peace and stability but remains economically intertwined with Tehran. On advanced chips, Washington also appeared to hold its line, despite Beijing’s interest in easing US technology restrictions. That may ultimately prove more consequential than the ceremonial theatrics. The summit thus produced no obvious quid pro quo in which China would use its leverage over Iran in return for a major American concession.Trump’s defenders argued though that the president’s approach should be judged against what they described as decades of failed China policy under previous administrations. “Obama and Biden talked tough, but gave away American factories to the Chinese. Trump actually launched a trade war against China,” noted Brian Kilmeade on Fox News, pointing out that Trump "kicked the Chinese out of Panama Canal" and went after their “favourite oil proxies in our hemisphere, Venezuela and Iran, and is about to kick them out of Cuba. ”That in essence is the larger contradiction of the summit. Trump has not abandoned confrontation with China; he has instead recast it as transactional management between two superpowers, much to the consternation of other nations like India, Japan, and South Korea. Xi, for his part, repeatedly spoke not of friendship between two men but of China and the US as “two major countries” with a responsibility to find a new way of coexisting.The symbolism was perhaps captured most neatly by the contrasting tours offered during the two leaders’ encounters. When Trump visited Beijing in May, Xi showed him ancient trees at Zhongnanhai, including specimens more than 1,000 years old — a quiet display of Chinese historical depth and long-term continuity. In Washington, Trump showed Xi his new White House helipad, built in a “record” 12 weeks – which the Chinese would have built in 12 days if not 12 hours.
Article Summary: Xi Jinping's 48-hour state visit to the United States yielded no immediate major breakthroughs but confirmed the broad impression, in visuals and much as words, that Washington now accepts China as a peer in a new G-2 formulation. A fawning Trump repeatedly described Xi as a friend and the relationship as a “great friendship,” with little personal reciprocity from the Chinese leader.

Article Title: ‘No Muslim can even dare’: Pakistan PM at UN condemns Houthi attacks, draws red line over Mecca
Article Text:
Pakistan's PM Shehbaz Sharif speaks at UNGA

NEW DELHI: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday used the 81st United Nations General Assembly to condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and warn against any threat to the safety and sanctity of Mecca.He also defended Pakistan’s new defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, while highlighting Islamabad’s diplomatic efforts to bring the United States and Iran to the negotiating table."We once again condemn, in the strongest possible terms, the recent deplorable attacks by the Houthis against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia," Sharif said in his address."The attempted drone attack on the holy city of Mecca al-Mukarramah has outraged Muslims across the globe. Any threat to safety and sanctity... is a red line that must never be crossed. No Muslim can even dare to think of committing such a heinous (act)."Saudi Arabia has accused the Houthis of targeting Mecca with a drone, an allegation the Houthis denied. Riyadh has also reported intercepting Houthi ballistic missiles following renewed hostilities in the region.Sharif also sought to underline Islamabad’s diplomatic role in the conflict between the United States and Iran, saying Pakistan had worked to bring the two sides to the negotiating table.“Pakistan chose to act swiftly through concerted efforts. Pakistan successfully brought Washington and Tehran under one roof in Islamabad. From the Islamabad talks to the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, many historic steps were taken to bring an end to this serious conflict,” he said.The Pakistani prime minister also referred to the recently signed defence agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement provides for collective defence commitments among the three countries, while Pakistani officials have said the arrangement is not directed against any particular state.Sharif said the pact was intended to serve defence, stability and peace rather than confrontation.On Palestine, Sharif denounced what he called Israel’s “genocidal agenda” and condemned what he described as “Israeli aggression against Lebanon and Syria”.He also thanked Pakistan’s Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff, Field Marshal Asim Munir, crediting his “relentless efforts” with helping create “space for diplomacy under exceptionally difficult and challenging circumstances”.Sharif further thanked US President Donald Trump for what he called his “timely intervention” during the 2025 India-Pakistan conflict, saying it had “saved hundreds of millions of lives in South Asia”.His remarks came as Pakistan balances its ties with Iran with its deepening strategic and defence relationship with Saudi Arabia, while regional tensions continue to test Islamabad’s stated preference for diplomacy.
Article Summary: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif used the 81st United Nations General Assembly to condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. He also defended Pakistan’s new defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, while highlighting Islamabad's diplomatic efforts to bring the United States and Iran to the negotiating table.

Article Title: All-women SIT to probe child rape case against Veeramani
Article Text:
Chennai police have established a Special Investigation Team to probe allegations of sexual offences against R Veeramani.





CHENNAI: Tamil Nadu govt has formed a four-member all-women IPS officers’ special investigation team (SIT) to probe the child rape case against the granite baron, R Veeramani, and other ‘related matters. ’The SIT will be headed by additional commissioner of police PC Thenmozhi of the Central Crime Branch in Chennai city police. The other members are: Joint commissioner of police N Disha Mittal of the West Zone, superintendent of police J Mutharasi, who handles spokesperson and media relations for the DGP's office, and deputy commissioner of police VV Geethanjali of the Central Women and Children (CWC) unit in Chennai city police.The arrest of Veeramani, and his two associates -- Shanthi and Mahendra Simhan -- on August 29 based on a video clipping showing the rape of a child rocked Tamil Nadu, as he was a leading industrialist who had headed several entities including India-Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry for several years.Police officers, on condition of anonymity, said at least nine more children had recorded their statements saying they too had been similarly raped.A long-time employee of Veeramani’s Gem Granites, Ganesan, too has been arrested for being in possession of video clippings of child rapes.Assistant commissioner of police Yasmin was shunted out of her present post as assistant commissioner of Koyambedu, as she was the one who filed a “further action dropped” report before a special court for Pocso cases and tried to close the case.The SIT has been tasked with probing the rape case as well as other “related matters” amidst political and social outcry over the suspected attempts to close the case under “further action dropped” category. Police have been examining evidence and statements collected during the investigation, including digital material linked to the case.The SIT will coordinate the investigation and examine the evidence and statements collected so far as part of the continuing probe.
Article Summary: Chennai police have established a Special Investigation Team to probe allegations of sexual offences against R Veeramani. The SIT has been tasked with probing the rape case as well as other ‘related matters’ amidst political and social outcry over the suspected attempts to close the case.

Article Title: Department of Labor IG Anthony D'Esposito hints at 'total shutdown' of H-1B visa program; says: 365 days from now ...
Article Text:
What Department of Labor IG Anthony D'Esposito said about H-1B visa

A widening investigation

The policy backdrop

Anthony D’Esposito, Inspector General at the Department of Labor, has hinted at a potential “total shutdown” of the H‑1B visa program within the next year. Speaking in Washington, D’Esposito said investigators are building a sweeping case against fraud in the foreign labor system, adding: “We have handcuffs ready… We are building a case. I think that the efforts and the focus that you see from the White House and from this administration is telling a story. We are laying out the case very vividly to the American people. l think that the foreign labor visa program is going to look very different 365 days from now than it does today."The remarks come amid an aggressive push by the Trump administration to tighten oversight of the H‑1B program, which allows U.S. employers to hire foreign workers in specialty occupations.In an interview with commentator Benny Johnson, D'Esposito warned that the H-1B program could look "very different" a year from now as the Trump administration steps up investigations into alleged foreign-labour fraud. Some outlets read his remarks as pointing to a total shutdown of the program, though his own words were that the system will look very different in 365 days.He also said his team has "handcuffs ready" for offenders.He described the effort as a deliberate, public case-building exercise. "We are laying out the case very vividly to the American people," he said, adding that the White House's focus tells its own story. He rejected the idea that this is routine compliance work, saying it is not a paperwork accounting issue and that "this is real."According to reports, the administration is expanding a nationwide investigation into alleged foreign labor fraud, worker exploitation and potential human trafficking. In a separate post, D'Esposito referred to alleged "fake employers," "sham jobs" and "visa mills," and the Labor Department's Office of Inspector General said on September 18 that it had issued dozens of subpoenas and executed search warrants in multiple locations.The office is also looking beyond H-1B. In a September 22 post, D'Esposito said his office is targeting colleges accused of exploiting J-1 visas, following the sponsors, grant money and people behind the scheme, and told fraudsters to expect cuffs.The enforcement push runs alongside other administration measures. A presidential executive order now requires federal agencies to assess whether employers seeking foreign petitions have recently laid off similarly situated American workers, and the administration has introduced a $100,000 fee for certain new offshore petitions, along with extended entry restrictions on some overseas H-1B recipients through September 2027. The White House has said the earlier restriction was followed by a 92 per cent decline in H-1B registrations from the largest US IT outsourcing firms.The Labor Department also launched a related enforcement effort last year. In September 2025 it announced Project Firewall, aimed at ensuring employers prioritize qualified Americans in hiring and holding them accountable for abusing the H-1B process.
Article Summary: Department of Labor IG Anthony D'Esposito hints at potential 'total shutdown' of H-1B program. He says investigators are building a sweeping case against fraud in the foreign labor system. Remarks come amid an aggressive push by the Trump administration to tighten oversight of the H- 1B program, which allows US employers to hire foreign workers.

Article Title: After months of AI tensions, Trump dines with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei
Article Text:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei

Dario Amodei previously warned about rapid AI development

US President Donald Trump had dinner with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Sunday, September 27, bringing the two together for a private meeting after months of disagreements between the Trump administration and the AI company over safety and the military use of its technology. As stated in an AP report, the dinner took place at the White House and was the first reported one-on-one meeting between Trump and Amodei. The meeting came just days after a federal appeals court backed the Pentagon’s decision to classify Anthropic as a supply chain risk, allowing the Defense Department to continue removing the company’s Claude AI models from its systems.Before the meeting, Trump told Fox News while attending the Presidents Cup golf tournament ​in Illinois “We're ​about maybe a year and a half up on China. We're leading, and we're building tremendous, trillions of dollars' worth of places. And why should we give ⁠that up?”As mentioned above, the dinner comes after a period of tension between Anthropic and the Trump administration over how AI should be developed and used by the US military. Anthropic has raised concerns about the use of AI for activities such as mass surveillance and autonomous weapons. Amodei has also called for the AI industry to slow down development so that safety measures can keep pace with increasingly powerful systems.Trump, meanwhile, has pushed for the US to maintain its lead in AI development, particularly in competition with China.Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has recently become one of the prominent voices calling for greater caution around advanced AI.Earlier this month, he warned that AI systems could become capable of leading large groups of AI agents and potentially taking control of major parts of the internet within six to 12 months if development continues without stronger safety measures.The meeting also comes ahead of a broader gathering of AI executives at the White House. Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson are expected to meet several major AI leaders this week, September 29.The dinner therefore brought together two figures who have publicly taken different positions on the pace and regulation of AI development, while the US government continues to debate how to balance AI innovation, national security and safety.
Article Summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei had dinner with US President Donald Trump on Sunday, September 27. The dinner was the first reported one-on-one meeting between the two. It comes after months of tension between Anthropic and the Trump administration over how AI should be developed and used by the US military.

Article Title: Watch: UK police robot targets vans near airbase used by US forces
Article Text:
Footage from Britain shows a bomb-disposal robot moving directly toward one of the suspicious vehicles in Whelford, near RAF Fairford, and carrying out a close inspection of the vehicle. (GIF: @ddfmarketing1)

Trump says suspects were ‘looking to do big damage’

A bomb-disposal robot was deployed around three suspicious vans near RAF Fairford, a British air base used by US bombers, after Gloucestershire Police arrested five men who were later held on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act.A video shared on X appeared to show the remotely operated machine moving around the vehicles near the Gloucestershire airfield. Aerial footage showed two vans with their rear doors open and large dark objects nearby, while the robot appeared to be trying to gain access to the third vehicle.Gloucestershire Police received a call at about 12.45am on Sunday about three suspicious vehicles apparently travelling towards RAF Fairford. Armed officers arrested five men in Whelford on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act. They were subsequently arrested on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act, with Counter Terrorism Policing taking over the investigation.Police imposed a 400-metre cordon around the vehicles while the Army's explosive ordnance disposal unit examined them. About 85 households were evacuated as a precaution. Gloucestershire Police said the immediate incident appeared to be contained.Police have not announced a motive. Reuters reported that investigators were giving greatest weight to a possible Iran link, while also examining whether Russian sabotage or an Islamist plot was involved, citing a person familiar with the inquiry.The five men remained in custody on Monday as police questioned them. Their nationalities have not been disclosed. Defence minister Wes Streeting said he would not speculate about the motive while the investigation was ongoing.The US president, Donald Trump, said the suspects had been “looking to do big damage”.“We had them under view for a long time, and we got them,” Trump told reporters in Chicago. He said British and American authorities had been investigating the men before their arrests.A local farmer told the Daily Telegraph she alerted police after encountering the vans and seeing several men, some with their faces covered, moving towards nearby fields.RAF Fairford hosts the headquarters of the US Air Force's 501st Combat Support Wing and the 420th Air Base Squadron. Britain had authorised US bombers based there to strike Iranian missile sites that were attacking shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.In July, Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned Britain against allowing US bombers to fly from Fairford, saying bases used to launch attacks could be treated as legitimate targets. Tehran has previously rejected claims that it was behind attacks or plots in the UK or other countries.Security was tightened around Fairford following the arrests. Measures were also increased at RAF Lakenheath and RAF Mildenhall, two other British bases used by US forces.Vicki Evans, senior national coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing, said officers were still gathering evidence and establishing the circumstances of the incident. Under the Terrorism Act 2000, the five men can be detained for up to 14 days without charge.
Article Summary: Five men arrested in Whelford, near RAF Fairford, on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act. US president Donald Trump says suspects were ‘looking to do big damage’ A bomb-disposal robot was deployed around three suspicious vans near the base.

Article Title: N Chandrasekaran, Narayana Murthy join Gurudevshri Rakeshji’s 60th, marked by 60 transformative initiatives
Article Text:
He said cultural transformation could hasten India’s journey towards a Viksit Bharat.





MUMBAI: India’s future will be shaped by the culture, character and quality of its people and leaders, Infosys founder NR Narayana Murthy said at spiritual guru Pujya Gurudevshri Rakeshji’s 60th birthday celebrations.He added cultural transformation could hasten India’s journey towards a Viksit Bharat.Some of India's most influential business leaders came together to honour Pujya Gurudevshri Rakeshji, founder of Shrimad Rajchandra Mission Dharampur (SRMD), on his 60th birth anniversary.The two-day Mumbai event saw launch of 60 projects, including a cancer hospital, university and animal hospital.On Saturday, Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran shared "I have now spent 40 years in the Tata Group. Strong values - trust, character, discipline, perseverance, and hard work, are what build great individuals and great institutions."Drawing a direct line between the Tata ethos and SRMD’s outreach, he added, "That is why the work of Gurudev is so meaningful. Through his teachings and his work with young people, these values and this sense of purpose are being shared with millions."Murthy recalled his mother feeding a poor child every night despite the family’s modest means: generosity, he said, needn't wait for abundance.Referring to the 60 initiatives showcased at the event, Murthy said, "The true measure of any spiritual tradition lies not just in its teachings, but in the compassion, it inspires through action.India's future will ultimately be shaped by the quality of its people.”Gurudevshri Rakeshji turned the spotlight away from the milestone. “What exactly are we celebrating today? A birthday, an individual or something else?” he asked.“Everyone receives 86,400 seconds daily. They cannot be saved, stored or transferred. Nor does changing surroundings necessarily change the mind. If you don’t change in the mind, you can be restless in Mumbai or London. That was why seva and sadhana remain relevant in a fast-paced world. Spirituality could mean learning to close the unnecessary apps of your mind, gaining control over words, reactions and instincts,” said Gurudevshri Rakeshji.On the occasion, Senior Sanyasi and SRMD vice president Atmarpit Nemiji dedicated “Beyond’, a new visual chronicle, to Gurudevshri Rakeshji.His guru, he said, defied conventional definitions of a relationship, He does not fit into a relationship. He becomes whatever the soul needs without ever changing who he is.
Article Summary: Infosys founder NR Narayana Murthy spoke at spiritual guru Pujya Gurudevshri Rakeshji's 60th birthday celebrations. He said cultural transformation could hasten India’s journey towards a Viksit Bharat. Two-day Mumbai event saw launch of 60 projects, including a cancer hospital, university and animal hospital.
